turns.query: I need in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs. I want predicted CLh (hepatic clearance mL/min/kg) and extraction ratio for each compound.
turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with compound_id, CLint_uL_per_min_mg (microsomal intrinsic clearance), and molecular_weight columns for your 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs (e.g., Imatinib, Dasatinib, Nilotinib, Bosutinib)
Key steps:

CLint scaling → MPPGL correction + plasma protein binding adjustment → predicted CLint,u (unbound)
Well-stirred model + parallel-tube model → CLh (mL/min/kg) per compound
Hepatic extraction ratio (EH = CLh / QH, where QH = 20.7 mL/min/kg) computed and flagged by tier


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh + EH per compound, both models) + clearance_summary.json (ranked compounds + model comparison)

Decision gate: Flag compounds with EH > 0.7 (high extraction, first-pass risk) for dose adjustment review, and EH < 0.3 (low extraction) as candidates for oral bioavailability optimization.

Decision gate: Compounds with EH > 0.7 (expected: Dasatinib) are flagged as high-extraction — first-pass effect risk, oral bioavailability likely <30%, dose escalation or IV formulation review required. Pharmacophore screen of 4-compound library → feature-match scoring per compound against the consensus model with min_features = 3 threshold applied


Expected output: filtered_hits.csv (compounds passing ≥3 feature matches with per-feature scores) + pharmacophore_model.json (feature definitions + coordinates) + ranked HTML report with 2D depictions and match annotations

Decision gate: Only compounds matching ≥ 3 pharmacophore features advance — expected hits: Gleevec-analog-1 (high match, structurally identical to Imatinib) and Ponatinib (known ABL1 inhibitor); Terfenadine and Acetaminophen are predicted to fail the threshold due to absent kinase-binding features.

Input: 30-row assay CSV (15 compounds × 2 assay types: IC50_BCR_ABL1 in nM + hERG_IC50 in µM, dated 2026-03-15)

CSV parse & unit normalization → pivoted compound × assay matrix (nM → µM conversion applied across assay types)
Composite scorer → weighted rank score: BCR-ABL1 potency (60%) + hERG safety margin (40%), log-scaled; flags compounds with hERG IC50 < 1 µM as cardiac risk
Report generator → ranked_compounds.csv + HTML dashboard with selectivity index (hERG IC50 / BCR-ABL1 IC50) per compound


Expected output: ranked_compounds.csv (rank, composite score, cardiac risk flag) + assay_summary.json (per-compound potency/safety breakdown) + interactive HTML report with compound tier classification (Tier 1: potent + safe; Tier 4: withdrawn-drug profile)

Decision gate: hERG IC50 < 1 µM → automatic cardiac risk flag (CPD003, CPD005, CPD009, CPD010 flagged); BCR-ABL1 IC50 < 1 nM + hERG IC50 > 10 µM → Tier 1 advancement (CPD004, CPD005, CPD006 candidates; CPD009/CPD010 rank last despite any potency due to hERG disqualification).
